description: The LICA thesis embraces instruction, learning, school-wide programming and social/community concerns, and the authors state \"Ten of the most fundamental\" recurring themes or guiding precepts.
title: Ten guiding precepts for school-wide languaging-oriented reading programs

description: Lightbody's (2017) framework structures equality in CEL around four interrelated elements: \"power-sharing and rep- resentation, partnerships, bureaucracy, and funding and resources\".
title: Lightbody's four-element framework of equality in community-engaged learning

description: The chapter contrasts two learning principles underlying lexical organization.
title: Principle of likely need versus principle of repetition as competing accounts of lexical learning

description: The article develops a coding typology distinguishing four \"limiting\" strategies, which \"may work well for well-structured, end-of-chapter exercises, but they begin to fail as the problems become more complex\" (Rolode...
title: Typology of limiting versus expansive problem-solving strategies in student reflections

description: The review presents two dueling hypotheses about English Language Learners' reading, discussed by Bernhardt and Kamil (1995).
title: Linguistic Threshold Hypothesis versus Linguistic Interdependence Hypothesis for ELL reading comprehension

description: The paper argues that although listening is classified as a receptive skill, it is not passive: \"Listeners do not passively absorb the words, but actively attempt to grasp the facts and feelings in what they hear\".
title: Listening as an active process of constructing meaning from a stream of sounds

description: The paper organizes listening skills into macro-language use, \"the learning of elements of language and their potential combinations\", and micro-skills that each perform different functions.
title: Taxonomy of macro- and micro-skills of listening comprehension

description: The article adopts Littlewood's model of advanced language learners' development, which divides communication needs into pragmatic needs, \"the desire to communicate effectively in a pragmatic sense\", and social needs,...
title: Littlewood's division of advanced learners' communication needs into pragmatic and social needs

description: The paper proposes a typology distinguishing four basic types of learning along two axes: whether the knowledge structure is pre-established or situational, and whether primary agency lies with teachers or learners.
title: Four-part typology of adult learning based on knowledge structure and primary agency
